summary: docs/BIOME_TRAITS.md section 7 (kill rewards) is implemented in PainterIO.Core and tested. Three new behaviour traits, one file each, with TraitDefaults rows and registry lines: KillInheritance (TraitId 9, Share 1.0, Share in [0, 1]), KillSpeedBoost (10, PerKill 0.10, Cap 0.30) and KillShield (11, Duration 3.0). They plug into the Simulation through a new optional companion interface IKillTrait (+ data class KillInfo); ISimTrait is unchanged. The 7.1 core rules are explicit and neutral in classic rounds: PlayerState.SpeedMultiplier (tick speed = PawnSpeed x SpeedMultiplier x the Conduction factor when home, read at tick start), Spark.Speed fixed at the cut to SimConfig.SparkSpeedOf(victim.SpeedMultiplier) (new SimConfig bool SparkFollowsVictimSpeed, default true; false = always the base spark speed) and used by every closed form, PlayerState.ExitWasCut (set with the spark, cleared at Exit / return / elimination and by the R14 cross-tick cancellation; a return with it captures nothing, Return.Chased = true), and PlayerState.ShieldEnd with an exact ShieldEnd candidate in section 6 (cut candidates are recomputed from that u, a head already over the trail cuts at that instant). Kill rewards run at the end of step b (the last step that can eliminate, so 'alive after step b' = 'alive after the group'), for every Spark elimination whose killer is alive, in kill order then TraitId order; events TerritoryInherited, SpeedBoosted, ShieldStarted, ShieldEnded are appended at the END of SimEventType (SimEvent gains Value). SimView gains SpeedMultiplier(i), EffectiveSpeed(i), IsShielded(i), ShieldEndTime(i); SparkCatchEta uses Spark.Speed. The HeadGrace check uses the maximum reachable speed (product of the speed traits' maxima: Conduction 1.3 x boost 1.3). StateHash adds the kill state only when a kill trait is attached (the D-1 sets keep their hashes). Section 7.2 consequences are implemented and tested: inheritance only for a surviving killer (else neutral + ScorchedEarth), an inherited cell under the killer's trailing head returns it at that instant (unchased captures, chased captures nothing), a chased killer that gets KillShield loses its spark and its loop stays lost. Bots per 7.2: no attack (lethal or denial) on a shielded enemy and abort when the victim becomes shielded, threats ignored and a longer trail allowed while their own shield lasts (bolder plans, depth x 1.4), go home once a shield extinguished their spark (the cut exit cannot pay), every speed estimate multiplied by SpeedMultiplier and the predicted spark by SparkSpeedOf(victim), and under KillInheritance the lethal cut value includes the victim's area (prefer the most valuable victim, draw AttackChance x min(1 + Share x victim cells / own cells, 1.5)). One real bug was found by the v1.1 balance rounds and fixed: when the kill leaves the trailing killer as last survivor (or happens in the TimeUp group) the round ended in the kill group before the same-instant return of the inherited cell under its head, leaving Home != owner(Cell); those returns are now applied before the round end check (regression test added). Classic stays bit-identical: the whole existing suite is green, the classic rolling hash 8CB763231AC73608 is reproduced (default config, SparkFollowsVictimSpeed true and false, all 11 traits disabled), the three kill traits at neutral parameters evolve exactly like classic at 30 / 60 / 144 Hz, and the player probe built from this tree prints [ProbeHash] 246577239DE179C4 at -fps 30 and at -fps 144 (its FAIL line is another package's new shader, see needs). dotnet loop (.art/kill-core): 510 / 510 green (443 before + 67 new executed cases, + 2 explicit diagnostic cases run on demand, green). Unity EditMode through the lock: 663 cases, 658 passed, 4 skipped (2 existing BotsReport, 2 explicit diagnostics), 1 failure outside this package (WaveC_Composites_KeepTheirFetchCount, liq-drop work); every kill and trait test class passes in Unity. Balance report re-run with the NEW defaults (section 3 + section 7) and with the D-1 proposals, lasso off (50 seeds) and on (20 seeds): see balance_report. Defaults NOT changed. Recommendation: apply both D-1 proposals (Liquide Inertia 480, Feu SparkSpeed 2.3): all five section 6 tendencies are then met lasso off AND on (v1.1 as is: 4/5 lasso off, 3/5 lasso on). Feu with KillInheritance is the strongest snowball as 7.2 predicted: an inheritance flips the lead in 74 % (off) / 80 % (on) of rounds and decides 48 % / 65 % of the TimeUp duels; Share 0.5 halves that swing (measured) if playtests find Feu too swingy.

contract_issues: Kill rewards timing (7, 'applied in the elimination step, before the round-end check'): implemented at the end of step b (the kill traits run right after the group's Spark eliminations, then the shield ends, then steps c-f). Equivalent to 'after the eliminating group' because only steps a and b eliminate. Event order per kill: SparkCaught, Eliminated, then TerritoryInherited / SpeedBoosted / ShieldStarted (kill order, then TraitId order). Implied amendment of section 6: a step 'b2 kill rewards' and a step 'b3 shield ends' between b and c.

Same-instant returns before a round end (7.2 'returns at that instant through the normal section 6 state check'): when a kill reward put a trailing killer's head on its own cell and the round ends in that same group (last survivor, or the TimeUp group), there is no later candidate pass, so the round used to end with Home != owner(Cell). Such returns are now applied with the step a rules right before the round end check (ReturnsBeforeRoundEnd, only in groups where kill rewards ran). Outcome = what the next pass would give (same time; the return's capture counts in FinalCells). Found by the balance rounds; regression test KillInheritance_ALastSurvivorTrailingOverTheInheritedLandReturnsBeforeTheRoundEnds.

Shield semantics as built: ShieldEnd is a candidate kind (u = max(uCur, (ShieldEnd - t0) / dt)), re-validated against an extension by a kill of the same group; ShieldEnded.Value = end time; a later kill re-emits ShieldStarted with the new end; an elimination ends a shield silently (no ShieldEnded); StepCuts re-checks the shield, so a cut grouped (within eps) with the kill that shields its victim is dropped; DebugForceCut is refused on a shielded trail. Duration 0 does nothing (no shield, no extinguished spark).

Reading to confirm (user): after a shield ends, a still-trailing player whose spark was extinguished can be cut again and gets a NEW spark (section 6 keeps 'trailing and WITHOUT a spark' literally; R11 'at most one spark per exit' becomes 'at a time' once a shield can extinguish one). Its loop stays lost either way (ExitWasCut). Tested by KillShield_AfterTheShieldACutExitCanBeCutAgain. The alternative (a cut exit stays uncuttable) is a one-line change.

Return.Chased now means ExitWasCut (contract 5.5 said 'had a spark'); identical in classic. Margin is 0 when KillShield had already extinguished the spark (no spark at the return): the runtime WHY line ('Rentre 0,4 s avant l'etincelle') must not print a 0 s margin in that case (ShieldStarted.Chased tells it).

KillSpeedBoost: the multiplier applies from the tick after the kill (speed is decided per tick in step 1, read at tick start), so the trait is tick-rate dependent like Conduction and turning (no cross-rate test; the 7.1 spark rule is cross-rate tested with a constant multiplier). The multiplier accumulates as min(1 + Cap, m + PerKill); SpeedBoosted is emitted only when it grows (nothing at the cap, so a fourth kill at the default parameters emits nothing).

KillInheritance Share < 1 (section 7 gives only the default 1.0): the killer inherits round(Share x n) of the n freed cells, those nearest the centroid of the victim's land (squared distance in cell units, ties by index): deterministic, rate independent, a solid core rather than speckle; the rest stays neutral (and scorched with ScorchedEarth). Share 0 = no inheritance. TerritoryInherited.Point = the victim's head at the kill. Inherited cells are first neutralized (Eliminated still lists them, so ScorchedEarth records them) then given to the killer in the same group; IsScorched is false for them because they are owned.

HeadGrace check: section 4 / 7.1 'maximum reachable speed' is implemented as PawnSpeed x the PRODUCT of every speed trait's MaxSpeedFactor (was the maximum, identical with a single speed trait). Electricite v1.1 reaches 1.69 x PawnSpeed at home.

StateHash: per-player SpeedMultiplier, ExitWasCut, ShieldEnd and Spark.Speed are hashed only when a kill trait is attached, so the D-1 trait sets keep their hashes (the classic hash is untouched in all cases). SimView.SparkCatchEta is now (L - S) / (Spark.Speed - PawnSpeed x SpeedMultiplier).

Bots (7.2, as built): shielded enemies are never targeted (lethal or denial) and an attack aborts when the victim becomes shielded; a bot whose own shield lasts more than 1 s ignores threats and may trail MaxTrailLength + shieldLeft x its speed, and a plan made while shielded is 1.4 x deeper; a bot whose spark was extinguished goes home at once (ExitWasCut, nothing left to capture); every estimate uses PawnSpeed x SpeedMultiplier and the predicted spark SparkSpeedOf(victim multiplier); under KillInheritance the lethal victim with the largest value 1 + Share x victim cells / own cells is preferred and drawn with AttackChance x min(value, 1.5). All neutral in classic rounds (bit-identical, verified).

Section 6 tendencies with the v1.1 defaults (section 3 + 7): lasso off 4/5 met (Liquide closest to classic MISSED: L 0.154 vs E 0.118); lasso on 3/5 (Feu kill share 38 % below Liquide 42 %, and Feu 3.95 cuts/round above Electricite 3.60). With the D-1 proposals (Liquide Inertia 480, Feu SparkSpeed 2.3) all 5 are met lasso off and on. Defaults NOT changed: the table lives in the Runtime BiomeTraitTable (user decision).

Swing measured as 7.2 asks (Feu v1.1): 1.5 inheritances per round of 14 to 17 % of the arena each; an inheritance flips the lead in 74 % (off) / 80 % (on) of rounds; 48 % / 65 % of TimeUp duels are won by less than the winner's largest single inheritance; mean final coverage 70.8 % (Feu section 3: 52.8 %, classic 41.5 %). Feu is by far the most decisive biome. Share 0.5 measured: decided-by-one-kill 39 % / 28 %, coverage 56.7 % / 57.8 %, but kill share 53 % and TimeUp only 82 % lasso off.

Main case (regular loop, asserts TimeUp >= 40 %): Classic + the v1.1 defaults. Explicit case TraitsBalance_Diagnostics: + D-1 proposals, section 3 sets, each kill trait alone, Feu Share 0.5. 'kill share' = SparkCaught / Cut; 'distance' = mean relative difference to classic over captures per bot, cuts, kill share, saved, coverage, eliminations, end time, cells per capture. Swing: 'lead flip' = a round where an inheritance made the killer the strict leader among the alive players; 'decided by one kill' = a TimeUp round with one winner whose margin over the best other survivor is below its largest single inheritance.

recommendation_not_applied: Liquide: Inertia 420 -> 480 (keep Coalescence 2.0 and KillShield 3.0). Restores 'Liquide closest to classic' in both lasso modes (0.154 -> 0.097 off, 0.200 -> 0.106 on) and brings its kill share from 42 % to 37-38 %.

Feu: SparkSpeed 2.1 -> 2.3 (keep Propagation 4/1, ScorchedEarth 15, KillInheritance). Not needed lasso off (v1.1 already meets all but the Liquide tendency) but required lasso on: Feu kill share 38 % -> 54 % and Electricite regains 'most cuts'. With both changes all five tendencies are met lasso off and on.

KillInheritance Share: keep 1.0 (the user's Paper.io 2 decision), but the swing is large (half of the TimeUp duels decided by one inheritance lasso off, two thirds lasso on). If playtests find Feu too swingy, Share 0.5 is the measured softer option (decided-by-one-kill 39 % / 28 %, coverage about 57 %), at the cost of more kills and fewer TimeUp rounds (82 % lasso off).

KillSpeedBoost 0.10 / 0.30 and KillShield 3.0: keep. Alone they are light (distance to classic 0.016 / 0.026); in their biomes Electricite moves closer to classic than its section 3 set (0.151 -> 0.118) and Liquide too (0.218 -> 0.154), and the shield gives about one comeback every five rounds.
